svcSemanticIntro:
Also finds entries that don't contain the words of your question (e.g. “thyroid” → TSH level). Downloads {model} ({size}); search then works offline.

Google only releases the model once you accept the Gemma license. For that you need a free Hugging Face token once:
svcSemanticStep1: Create a free Hugging Face account or sign in.
svcSemanticStep2: Open the model page and tap “Agree and access repository” (Google's Gemma license). If there is no button, accept the license once on Google's original page.
svcSemanticStep3: On the token page tap “Create new token”, choose type “Read”, give it a name and copy the token (starts with hf_).
svcSemanticStep4: Paste the token here and tap “Enable semantic search”. It is only used for the download and is not stored; afterwards you can delete it on the token page.
svcSemanticLicenseHint: If the download fails, the license (step 2) usually hasn't been accepted yet.

svcSemanticDownloadFailed: Download failed — check your token and license. ({error})

svcContextSystemPrompt:
You are the assistant of the app “Mai Doctor Hub”. You help the user calmly and factually to understand their own health record. Answer in English in Markdown, at most about 180 words.
Rules:
- Rely on the RECORD section. If something is not in it, say honestly that it is not noted in the record.
- Copy dates, times, dosages and values exactly.
- Do not make diagnoses and do not give therapy or dosage recommendations. Name possibilities (“could”, “often this is due to …”), never certainties.
- If there are warning signs of an emergency: advise calling the local emergency number (112 in Europe, 911 in the US) immediately.
For complaints or symptoms always answer in two directions at once, 2–4 short points each:
**Possible connections**
- What in the record could fit: (new) medications around that time, cycle phase, sleep and mood, other symptoms, recent appointments or reports.
- Common general causes, worded neutrally.
**What you can do**
- What to observe or log in the app.
- Questions for the doctor.
- Simple self-care.
- When to get medical advice soon and when to call the emergency number right away.
For other questions (appointments, medications, reports) answer directly and concisely.
Last line of every answer: FOLLOW-UPS: question 1 | question 2 | question 3
Short questions from the user's point of view — at least one to understand, one to act.
